title: [Peek] Add extensible codec support for professional video formats such as ProRes and DNxHD/DNxHR
author: HEX962

status.label: Requires product and dependency direction
status.detail: A fallback media stack would introduce licensing, package-size, security, and servicing decisions beyond an issue-level fix design.

next_action.label: Obtain maintainer direction
next_action.reason: Choose whether PowerToys should own or permit a non-Media-Foundation decoder before implementation design.

judgment.rationale: The requested fallback decoder is technically motivated but cannot become an implementation-ready dashboard fix until maintainers approve a codec, dependency, packaging, and security model.
evidence: Peek currently creates Windows.Media.Core.MediaSource instances and queries installed decoders through CodecQuery.
The requested ProRes and DNxHD/DNxHR support is not available through the reporter's installed Media Foundation codecs.
PowerToys contribution guidance requires PM review for non-MIT dependencies and careful dependency management.
judgment.recommended_action: Route the proposal through maintainer product and dependency review before any engineering design or approval action.

issue_context.summary: Peek cannot decode several professional editing codecs through its native Media Foundation path, and the proposal asks for an optional fallback decoder.
known_information: A ProRes 422 Standard MOV opens in Peek's media UI but fails with a missing-codec identifier.
Peek's VideoPreviewer uses MediaSource and CodecQuery rather than DirectShow codec packs.
The request explicitly recognizes licensing, package-size, and security concerns.
inferences: Adding an FFmpeg-based or extensible decoder would materially expand Peek's attack surface and servicing obligations.
A supported external codec-extension route may be lower risk than bundling decoders, but that is a product decision rather than a confirmed solution.
issue_context.analysis: The reporter has already supplied enough technical context; the missing inputs belong to maintainers, not the author. Until dependency and isolation policy is selected, a code-level design would be speculative.
initial_investigation: Reviewed PowerToys dependency and license guidance in doc/devdocs/development/guidelines.md.

information_gaps.information: Approved decoder ownership, license, packaging, update, and sandbox model
information_gaps.why_needed: These decisions determine whether the feature is acceptable and which architecture can be designed safely.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Resolve through PowerToys maintainer and PM dependency review.
